blocks.x: Cloud, Edge & Platform applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Banking & Financial Services, cloud, edge & platform engineering builds the runtime for everything else we do: hybrid and multicloud architecture, cloud-native modernization of legacy estates, edge and distributed infrastructure for latency-critical operations, sre and reliability engineering, internal developer platforms, finops, and mission-critical high-performance systems. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: hybrid & multicloud architecture, cloud-native & legacy modernization, edge computing & distributed infrastructure — delivered on Dataq Forge and Dataq Twinverse with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Core estate inertia

Mainframe-adjacent cores and change freezes make every product launch a negotiation. Meanwhile cloud spend grows without unit economics — nobody can state cost per payment processed or per account opened.
KYC and periodic-review backlog

Customer due diligence refresh cycles lag behind actual risk changes; files queue for weeks in review pools while remediation backlogs grow. Manual file assembly across registries, screening tools and core systems consumes analyst hours that produce no judgment.
GenAI stuck between pilot and policy

Generative assistants for credit memos, research summaries and client drafts stall in model-risk review because guardrails, provenance and audit trails were not designed in. Shadow AI fills the gap, creating exactly the exposure the review was meant to prevent.

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: MiCA and Basel III endgame / capital regimes. Model quality and data lineage directly affect RWA and capital. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Programs run on a fixed rhythm so progress is visible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
